stories.headline: Binance loses ~$6.3B in largest crypto theft ever; TRM and Chainalysis blame North Korea

key_facts.fact: An attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains on October 29, 2026, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC, according to TRM Labs.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC. That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025

key_facts.fact: TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, the North Korean state-sponsored unit the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack; Chainalysis independently reached the same conclusion after seeing Binance funds commingle with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit.
key_facts.excerpt: TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack. Chainalysis said it saw Binance funds commingling with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit

key_facts.fact: Binance linked the theft to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop that let attackers access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals; Co-CEO Richard Teng said it 'involved a more complex attack process' and was not a single one-click action.
key_facts.excerpt: the access let attackers submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions after they accessed a service container, and it hasn't yet found evidence of a leaked wallet private key. 'To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action.'

key_facts.fact: Tether froze more than 1.567 billion USDT and Circle froze more than 800 million USDC tied to the incident; Aave froze its DAO-operated lending markets to stop the hacker from borrowing.
key_facts.excerpt: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the stablecoin firm froze more than 1.567 billion USDT, while Circle's Jeremy Allaire said it has frozen more than 800 million USDC associated with the incident.

key_facts.fact: Binance pledged to cover all losses, suspended withdrawals, and said it reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the theft, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover losses, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.

key_facts.fact: Chainalysis said about $2.8 billion of the stolen funds had been frozen so far and that attackers were using automated laundering patterns not seen before.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately $2.8 billion has been frozen so far... we are observing laundering patterns we have not seen before. Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation

key_facts.fact: Elliptic's Tom Robinson said that if North Korea is behind it, this one theft would almost double everything the regime has stolen in crypto to date.
key_facts.excerpt: "If North Korea is behind it, this one theft would almost double everything the regime has stolen in crypto to date."

stories.headline: Limpet mines hit tanker in Hormuz as Trump says Iran war will be 'wrapped up soon'

key_facts.fact: A small boat attached two limpet mines to the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, causing an engine-room fire, the first successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the US war with Iran began in February, maritime sources told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: A small boat attached two limpet mines to the hull of a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz causing a fire in its engine room and temporarily disabling the vessel, in the first successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the US war with Iran began in February

key_facts.fact: UKMTO said the incident occurred 25 nautical miles northeast of Oman's Khasab; the crew was safe and the vessel continued to its next port. Ukraine had hit the same tanker with naval drones in July over alleged Russian shadow-fleet work.
key_facts.excerpt: The incident occurred on Thursday, 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab, UKMTO said... Ukrainian forces also hit the Louise 1 in July with naval drones in the Black Sea

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC Navy said on Friday two oil tankers were stopped south of Hormuz after ignoring radio warnings and using an 'unauthorized route', and Iran said it destroyed a US unmanned vessel in the eastern strait, with no immediate US confirmation.
key_facts.excerpt: two oil tankers were involved in incidents and stopped in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz, after ignoring radio warnings and attempting to use what it described as an unauthorized route... Iran also said on Friday that it destroyed a US unmanned vessel

key_facts.fact: Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO on Friday that the Iran war is 'going to get wrapped up soon' and that the US needs 'a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon'.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's going to get wrapped up soon," Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO. "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon," he added.

key_facts.fact: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday in talks coordinated with Washington; Washington wants nuclear issues included from the start while Tehran demands the US first end its port blockade and lift oil export sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday as part of efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran... Washington wants nuclear issues included from the start of negotiations. Tehran demands that the US first end its port blockade and lift oil export sanctions.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper said US forces had cleared the strait's primary shipping routes of Iranian mines and that more than 50,000 US service members support operations across the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: Cooper said US forces had cleared the strait's internationally recognized primary shipping routes of Iranian sea mines... more than 50,000 US service members were supporting operations across the Middle East

stories.headline: ECB holds at 2.5% after debating a hike; Lagarde to leave nine months early

key_facts.fact: The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on October 29 after a 25 basis point hike in September, with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, its highest since September 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, as expected, after raising it by 25 basis points in September... Inflation has climbed to 3.8%, its highest since September 2023, driven by energy prices.

key_facts.fact: Lagarde said the Governing Council debated whether a hike was appropriate but unanimously decided to hold; money markets priced a 67% chance of a December hike.
key_facts.excerpt: "actually, the Governing Council debated whether a hike was appropriate... the Governing Council unanimously decided that we were well positioned enough at this stage to hold"... money markets priced in a 67% chance of a December hike

key_facts.fact: The ECB statement said energy prices have continued to rise, posing upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth, and that financing conditions have tightened since the last meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Energy prices have continued to rise, posing upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to the growth outlook... Financing conditions have tightened since our last meeting

key_facts.fact: Lagarde, 70, informed the Governing Council she will step down on February 7, 2027; her eight-year term was due to end October 31, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Lagarde, 70, will leave Feb. 7, the ECB said Thursday. Her eight-year term was to end Oct. 31, 2027.

key_facts.fact: At the press conference Lagarde said she was leaving to have 'the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters'.
key_facts.excerpt: Lagarde said: "I want to have the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters."

key_facts.fact: Danske Bank named Klaas Knot of the Netherlands and Pablo Hernandez de Cos of Spain as the two main government-endorsed candidates to succeed her.
key_facts.excerpt: The two main government-endorsed candidates to replace her are Klaas Knot of the Netherlands, whom we see as a pragmatic hawk, and Pablo Hernández de Cos of Spain, whom we see as a moderate dove.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, says inflation target met for the first time since 2013

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at 1.25%, the highest since 1995, on Friday, October 30, in an 8-1 vote; board member Hajime Takata dissented in favor of a hike to 1.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995. The decision was split 8-1, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting. Takata had wanted the bank to hike its policy rate to 1.5%.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ said underlying inflation is 'generally consistent' with its 2% target, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Japan declared that underlying inflation in the country was "generally consistent" with its target of 2%, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ raised its fiscal 2027 core inflation forecast to 2.6% from 2.4% and said price risks are skewed to the upside; its projections assume Dubai crude falls from about $105 to about $70 a barrel.
key_facts.excerpt: The board's median forecast for core inflation, which excludes fresh food, was raised to 2.6% for fiscal 2027 from 2.4% previously... Its projections assume Dubai crude falls from around $105 a barrel to around $70

key_facts.fact: The BOJ will raise ETF sales to about 860 billion yen a year from January 2027, cutting the time to unwind its holdings to about 43 years from about 112.
key_facts.excerpt: ETF sales will rise to about 860 billion yen a year from January 2027, cutting the disposal timeline to about 43 years from about 112

key_facts.fact: The decision closed a week in which the ECB, the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand all left rates unchanged; the yen strengthened to 157.115 per dollar.
key_facts.excerpt: The yen strengthened to a high of 157.115 per dollar... The BOJ wraps up a week of central bank decisions, with the European Central Bank, the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand all leaving interest rates unchanged

stories.headline: Alphabet loses record ~$500B in worst day ever on negative cash flow, dragging Nasdaq 1.4%

key_facts.fact: Alphabet shares fell about 13% on Thursday, October 29, the biggest drop since Google went public in 2004, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market value and passing the previous record decline of 11.63% from March 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap... passing the previous record of 11.63% set in March 2020.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for Q3, versus the $2.7 billion analysts expected, while keeping 2026 capex guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, compared to the $2.7 billion analysts expected. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's market value fell to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before, after it said its AI Mode was eating into search ad revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: By the end of Thursday, the company's total stock market value had fallen to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before.

key_facts.fact: The Nasdaq composite fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days, even though most stocks rose.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days, even though the wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4%

key_facts.fact: It was Alphabet's second straight quarter of negative free cash flow, something it had never seen before as a public company; net profit fell 25% to $26.2 billion, including an $8.7 billion loss on its SpaceX stake.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to $26.2bn... Alphabet booked an $8.7bn loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX

key_facts.fact: Microsoft traded largely flat; it reported $45.2 billion in capex and finance leases, below projections of $50.67 billion, with free cash flow down 27% but positive at $18.63 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter... below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive.

stories.headline: Pentagon refers fired Iran war planner Lt. Gen. Sylvia to DOJ over alleged leaks

key_facts.fact: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Joint Staff's director for strategy, plans and policy (J5), who was coordinating the Iran battle plan; no replacement has been named.
key_facts.excerpt: Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, and was coordinating the Iran battle plan... No replacement for Sylvia has been named.

key_facts.fact: On Thursday the Pentagon said it had made a criminal referral to the Justice Department in the alleged leak case, saying the ouster was necessary 'to protect sensitive information'.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon said Thursday that it has made a criminal referral in an alleged leak case, claiming the ouster of a top general was necessary "to protect sensitive information."

key_facts.fact: A Pentagon official said Sylvia was accused of leaking classified information on the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars and failed three polygraph tests; two other Pentagon sources told CBS the accusations are not true.
key_facts.excerpt: Sylvia failed three polygraph tests about sharing classified information with the press, the official said... Two other Pentagon sources confirmed to CBS News that the firing was related to the polygraph tests, but said those accusations are not true.

key_facts.fact: An internal Air Force OSI report seen by Axios said Sylvia admitted leaking classified information about Ukraine and Iran to two reporters over about a year, starting as early as June 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon's top military planner admitted to leaking classified information about Ukraine and Iran to two reporters from separate outlets over a one-year period, according to an internal report of the investigation shared with Axios.

key_facts.fact: The Joint Staff retracted an earlier statement thanking Sylvia for his 32 years of service; the firing comes as Trump weighs resuming strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms.
key_facts.excerpt: After initially issuing a statement extending "the deepest gratitude" for Slyvia's 32 years of service, a spokesperson for the Joint Staff retracted the statement... Sylvia's firing comes as President Trump weighs resuming strikes against Iran after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

stories.headline: Israel's final count: Netanyahu bloc wins 53 seats, loses majority; Arab parties take record 19

key_facts.fact: Israel's Central Elections Committee completed the count of Tuesday's election on Thursday: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 Knesset seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, and Arab-led parties 19, so no camp reached the 61 needed to govern.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc won 53 seats in Israel's 120-member Knesset... The bloc supporting Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, won 48 seats... neither secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu's bloc fell well below the 68 seats it controlled at its peak in the previous parliament.
key_facts.excerpt: well below the 68 it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament

key_facts.fact: Likud won 27 seats and Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party 21; the Arab parties' 19 seats nearly double their previous total.
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party won 27, followed by 21 seats for the opposition's centrist Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Two other Arab parties... winning a total of 19 seats. That figure is nearly double the number they had before the election.

key_facts.fact: More than 5.7 million people voted; 306,679 votes went to parties that failed to cross the electoral threshold.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 5.7 million people voted, and 25,789 ballots were disqualified. Another 306,679 votes went to parties that failed to cross the electoral threshold

key_facts.fact: Results will be certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, who will then choose a candidate to try to form a government; Netanyahu remains in charge meanwhile.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations... lie ahead... Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, remains in charge.
